supersedes.scope: current live-volume-core topology and Chilko rendered evidence only; the original review remains the historical pilot record

architecture.problem: The live rapid surface is a detail overlay, not a transmitting river volume. Forcing it to near-opaque coverage made both cold-water reaches read as pale sheets. The first Chilko core pilot also multiplied its topology by bank-feather alpha and exposed an artificial one-cell dry strip beside the sampled wet bank when reused on Terminator.
architecture.retained_solution: A second non-colliding solver-conforming mesh supplies Single Layer Water optical depth. Lateral topology accepts only quads whose four corners are wet, reaching the complete sampled wet bank without entering a dry cell. An independent 0.60 station-coverage threshold clips the rectangular moving-window ends. The mesh sits 1 cm beneath the live detail surface and reuses the raft-floor transmission aperture.
architecture.rollout_scope: Futaleufu Terminator and Chilko Lava Canyon only. Existing versioned maps migrate from their unique cooked-field identities; future regeneration persists bEnableLiveSolverVolumeCore. Colorado and Pacuare remain on their separately reviewed carriers.
architecture.lateral_core_rule: all four sampled cell vertices must be wet

futaleufu_terminator.verdict: retain: the water changes from warm chalk-gray to a transmitting blue-gray body and the rejected bank-parallel dry strip is absent; the large rapid highlight remains too bright for photoreal acceptance

chilko_lava_canyon.verdict: retain: the refined lateral topology preserves the blue-gray volume and rapid lace while reaching the sampled wet bank; no rectangular moving-window core end is visible
